newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Frenchman may miss Mir flight after latest mishap.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman may miss Mir flight after latest mishap.

text.p: French astronaut Leopold Eyharts seems likely to miss spending August in orbit after the latest mishap aboard Russia's Mir space station, Russian and West European officials said on Friday.

Alain Fournier-Sicre, European Space Agency mission chief in Russia, told Reuters that Eyharts' scientific projects on Mir would be thwarted if the present crew failed to fix the station's power supply before the Frenchman arrived.

Mir's deputy mission director Sergei Krikalyov told reporters at Mission Control outside Moscow it was "very likely" a meeting of officials on Monday would decide to stand down the present, accident-prone, crew and leave the repair work to the two Russians due to blast off with Eyharts on August 5.

Since Eyharts was only planning to be on Mir for three weeks, the wait for the repairs to power cables -- which were cut when the station's Spektr module was punctured in a collision on June 25 -- would render his mission all but pointless.
"To conduct a scientific mission on board Mir for the French astronaut might be difficult if this electrical connection is not made prior to the arrival of the new crew," Fournier-Sicre said.
"Most of the French equipment is located in the Priroda...And to restore the operation of the Priroda module, they need to perform the electrical connection in Spektr."
In Paris, France's national space agency, the CNES, said it may have to postpone Eyharts' mission to early next year.

"If it is the new Russian relief team due to reach the station in early August which carries out the repair, the French astronaut's flight would be delayed to January-February 1998," CNES director-general Gerard Brachet told a news conference.
Mir mission director Vladimir Solovyov told reporters: "Eyharts is a good guy. He is capable of doing many things. But we must carefully look at the programme."

If repairs are put off after Thursday's crew error, which left the station spinning in darkness and all but out of control for 24 hours, it will be up to the experienced relief Russian cosmonauts Pavel Vinogradov and Anatoly Solovyov to mend Mir.
